Creative and office tools

Experiment 1

Documents, spreadsheets, slides and image editing

Aim

Design a professional technical document in LibreOffice Writer, build an automated calculation sheet in Calc, and perform layer masking, colour adjustment and export in GIMP.

  • LibreOffice Writer
  • Calc
  • Impress
  • GIMP

What I did

  1. Writer: laid out a résumé with a clear heading hierarchy, a sidebar, a cropped photo and formatted sections.
  2. Calc: built a T.E. Computer Engineering report card for 10 students, with totals out of 500, percentages and grades calculated by formulas.
  3. Also laid out the class timetable and a January 2026 calendar.
  4. Impress: made a six-slide introduction deck covering intro, about, skills, projects, responsibility and contact.
  5. GIMP: kept the original on a duplicate layer, applied colour adjustments and compared original against enhanced.

Output

Conclusion. Four open-source tools were chained into one workflow, from a written document to calculated data, a presentation and an edited image.

Experiment 2

Video editing in Shotcut and 3D modelling in Blender

Aim

Build a three-clip video sequence with sound transitions in Shotcut, then model and render a low-poly 3D object from scratch in Blender.

  • Shotcut
  • Blender

What I did

  1. Shotcut: imported three clips and an audio track, and placed the clips one after another on track V1.
  2. Overlapped each clip with the previous one by 1 to 2 seconds to create automatic cross-dissolve and audio crossfade transitions.
  3. Tuned the audio transition and added fade in and fade out filters, then exported with an H.264 preset.
  4. Blender: started from a cube or ico sphere and shaped it in Edit Mode with extrude, inset, scale and loop cut.
  5. Set Shade Flat, roughness 0.8, a Sun light and a camera, then rendered a 1920 × 1080 frame with F12.

Output

Conclusion. Both pipelines ran end to end: non-linear video editing in Shotcut and mesh modelling through to a render in Blender.

Version control and open collaboration

Experiment 3

Local Git: commits, branches and a merge conflict

Aim

Initialize a local Git repository, track files, make descriptive commits, create branches and resolve a simulated merge conflict.

  • Git
  • GitHub
  • VS Code

What I did

  1. Created the repository and made the first commit of config.txt.
  2. Branched to feature/update-config and set ENABLE_FEATURE_X=true.
  3. Returned to main and committed ENABLE_FEATURE_X=false, so both branches changed the same line.
  4. Merged the feature branch, which stopped with a conflict.
  5. Removed the conflict markers, kept the intended value, committed the merge and checked git log --graph.

Key commands

git init
git add config.txt
git commit -m "initial: create basic configuration file"
git checkout -b feature/update-config
git commit -am "feat: enable feature X in configuration"
git checkout main
git merge feature/update-config   # CONFLICT in config.txt
git add config.txt
git commit -m "merge: resolve feature X configuration conflict"
git log --oneline --graph

Output

Conclusion. Staging and committing create clean snapshots, branches isolate feature work, and a conflict is resolved by choosing the final state by hand.

Experiment 4

GitHub: SSH, fork, clone and pull request

Aim

Link local Git with GitHub, fork a public repository, clone it, push changes and file a formal pull request.

  • Git
  • GitHub
  • SSH
  • VS Code

What I did

  1. Generated an Ed25519 SSH key, added the public key to GitHub and tested with ssh -T.
  2. Forked the public repository and cloned the fork over SSH.
  3. Added the original project as the upstream remote and created feature/docs-update.
  4. Edited README.md, committed with a clear message and pushed the branch to origin.
  5. Opened a pull request from the fork to the original project with a title and description.

Key commands

ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "your_email@example.com"
ssh -T git@github.com
git clone git@github.com:YOUR-USERNAME/PUBLIC-REPO-NAME.git
git remote add upstream git@github.com:ORIGINAL-OWNER/PUBLIC-REPO-NAME.git
git checkout -b feature/docs-update
git commit -m "docs: add contribution guide notes to README"
git push -u origin feature/docs-update

Output

Conclusion. SSH keys secure the connection, a fork gives a safe place to work, and a pull request opens the change to review and integration.

Experiment 5

Editing Wikipedia: account, sandbox and citations

Aim

Create a verified Wikipedia account, practise editing in the sandbox, fix citation styling and expand a live stub article.

  • Wikipedia
  • MediaWiki
  • Wikitext

What I did

  1. Registered an account and confirmed the email address.
  2. Opened the user sandbox and practised bold, italics and headings in wikitext.
  3. Added inline citations with the Citation Style 1 template and a References section with reflist, then checked them with Show preview.
  4. Searched the stub categories for an article to expand with two or three sourced sentences and an edit summary.

Key commands

{{cite web |url=https://example.com |title=Example Title |publisher=Example Source |date=2026-01-01 |access-date=2026-08-21}}

== References ==
{{reflist}}

Output

Conclusion. Sandbox practice builds fluency in wikitext and citation standards before touching live pages, where verifiability and a neutral tone are the rules.

Linux, systems and virtualization

Experiment 6

Linux shell: navigation and text pipelines

Aim

Navigate with cd, ls and pwd, and process text with grep, awk, cat and the pipe operator.

  • Ubuntu
  • Bash
  • grep
  • awk

What I did

  1. Used pwd, ls -lah and cd with absolute and relative paths to move around the file system.
  2. Created a shell-practical folder and a students.txt file with ten records.
  3. Numbered lines with nl and filtered the IT students with grep.
  4. Extracted the name and marks columns with awk, then joined grep and awk with a pipe.

Key commands

pwd
ls -lah /
cd /var/log && cd ../..
grep -i "error" server.log
awk '{print $1, $2, "-->", $3}' server.log
grep "IT" students.txt | awk '{print $2, $4}'

Output

Conclusion. Small tools chained with pipes filter and reshape raw text without temporary files.

Experiment 7

System administration: permissions and background installs

Aim

Change file permissions and ownership with chmod and chown, and run software installation in the background with package managers.

  • Ubuntu
  • chmod
  • chown
  • apt
  • nohup

What I did

  1. Read the permission model: r=4, w=2, x=1 for owner, group and others.
  2. Created testfile.txt, set it to 600 with chmod and confirmed ownership with chown.
  3. Refreshed the package lists with apt update.
  4. Installed tree and checked its version.
  5. Wrote setup.sh, made it executable and ran it as a background job with &.

Key commands

chmod 600 testfile.txt
sudo chown ubuntu:ubuntu testfile.txt
sudo chmod -R 750 /opt/sysapp
DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive nohup sudo apt-get install -y nginx curl git > /var/log/sysapp/install.log 2>&1 &
jobs -l
ps aux | grep -E "apt|yum|dnf"

Output

Conclusion. Minimal permissions apply least privilege, and non-interactive flags with background jobs allow installs that run unattended.

Experiment 8

Virtualization and containers: VirtualBox and Docker

Aim

Deploy a guest Linux OS inside Oracle VirtualBox, then pull, build, launch and monitor an isolated application with the Docker CLI.

  • VirtualBox
  • Ubuntu
  • Docker
  • nginx

What I did

  1. Created an Ubuntu 64-bit VM with 2 CPUs, 4096 MB RAM and a dynamically allocated virtual disk.
  2. Installed Docker inside the guest and pulled the nginx image.
  3. Wrote a Dockerfile that serves a custom page and built it as my-web-app.
  4. Ran the container with port 8080 mapped to 80 and opened it in Firefox.
  5. Checked state and resource use with docker ps and docker stats.

Key commands

docker pull nginx:alpine
docker run -d --name my-isolated-web -p 8080:80 --memory="256m" --cpus="0.5" nginx:alpine
docker ps
docker stats my-isolated-web --no-stream
sudo docker build -t my-web-app .
sudo docker run -d --name my-web-container -p 8080:80 my-web-app

Output

Conclusion. VirtualBox isolates the whole machine, while Docker isolates only the application using kernel namespaces and cgroups, which is lighter and quicker to start.

Web deployment

Experiment 9

Web deployment: Apache, MySQL and WordPress

Aim

Install and verify a local Apache server, then set up a working multi-page site by installing WordPress on a local LAMP or WAMP stack.

  • XAMPP
  • Apache
  • MySQL
  • PHP
  • WordPress

What I did

  1. Installed XAMPP and started Apache and MySQL from the control panel.
  2. Opened phpMyAdmin and created the wordpress_db database.
  3. Extracted WordPress into htdocs and ran the web installer with the database details.
  4. Turned on pretty permalinks and created the Home, About us, Services and Contact pages.
  5. Built the menu and applied the Astra theme to the TechNova site, which includes a contact form.

Output

Conclusion. A local stack gives a safe place to build and test a full dynamic site, with Apache serving requests, PHP running the logic and MySQL storing the content.
